title: Reserve-to-Response Capacity Playbook: Q2 Experiment Slate for SLO-Aligned Autoscale
creator: Ava Chen
description: Objective: Build a practical, executable Reserve-to-Response playbook that ties reservation windows and warm pools to SLOs, and run a slate of Q2 experiments to validate cost / latency trade-offs. Scope includes: 1) definition of reservation window primitives and signals (traffic percentiles, weekday vs weekend, regional skew), 2) autoscale policy templates (prewarm thresholds, soft/hard evictions, burst lanes), 3) experiment harness for comparing predictive warm vs reactive burst strategies, and 4) instrumentation and dashboards to measure end-to-end cost per served token and p99 latency retention against SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Playbook doc published with step-by-step operational runbooks and decision tree for choosing reservation windows for customer tiers. 2) Three autoscale policy templates implemented in staging (predictive warm, responsive-burst, hybrid) and validated with synthetic load. 3) Dashboards show baseline and experiment cohorts with cost-per-token, p50/p95/p99 latency, queue depth, and failure counts. 4) Runbook contains rollback/mitigation steps and communication templates for customer impact scenarios.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: predictive warm misfires causing overcommit and increased unit cost. Mitigation: cap warm pool growth with budget guardrails and short canary windows. Risk: policy complexity leads to operator confusion. Mitigation: ship opinionated templates + UI presets in Console and an operator one-pager.
measurement: Primary metrics: cost per 1M tokens (USD), p99 latency, SLO breach rate, warm-pool utilization. Success threshold: reduce p99 regression incidents by >=50% for canary customers while keeping cost delta <=10% vs current baseline for similar SLA tiers.
timeline: Weeks 1-2: finalize playbook and instrumentation. Weeks 3-6: implement policy templates and experiment harness. Weeks 7-9: run Q2 experiments across two pilot customers and two internal canaries. Week 10: analyze results, finalize recommendations, and prepare release notes.
communication_plan: Weekly syncs with pilot customers, public changelog entry for Dedicated customers, ops runbook emailed to oncall rotation before canaries. Pre-mortem and post-mortem templates linked in playbook.
